guard.notes: .agents/hooks.json registers a PreToolUse hook that runs bun .guardrails/src/antigravity-hook.ts with AGENT_RUNTIME=antigravity. Antigravity uses a JSON contract instead of exit codes: the hook receives a camelCase payload on stdin (toolCall: {name, args}) and returns a verdict on stdout ({"decision":"allow"|"deny", "reason": ...}). The wrapper translates this to the guard's contract by spawning .guardrails/src/cli.ts evaluate and mapping exit 0 to allow and exit 2 to deny. The wrapper always exits 0: when bun or the guard is unavailable it prints no decision, and Antigravity applies its own default policy (fail-open).

capabilitiesNotes: The Antigravity CLI (agy) documents headless runs (agy -p), resume by conversation id (--conversation) and --output-format json with a usage envelope; none of this has been exercised in this repository yet, so every capability stays unknown until the first run. Hook payloads carry snake_case tool names (run_command, view_file, edit_file, write_file, replace_file_content, list_directory, code_action, search_web); the wrapper maps them to guard tool names. Skills are read natively from .agents/skills and global ~/.gemini/config/skills.
pricingNotes: No rates are recorded for this vendor; Google pricing sources are a follow-up.

permissions.notes: Reads and writes go through the host's own permission prompt (MCP tools run in Ask mode by default); shell runs on top of the guard policy via the .agents/hooks.json PreToolUse hook. Structural changes to roles, agents or skills, destructive actions and releases always need explicit user approval, in every mode.
